results.note: The migration adds `origin text not null default 'live'` and the checksum was updated. The module-scoped `postgres` fixture (test_persist.py:75-79) runs every migration against a real Postgres schema. The unmarked test at :180 then inserts and reads `origin`, so the schema change is exercised for real. The text check at :168 also passes.

Because the column is `NOT NULL DEFAULT 'live'` (migration line 2), every existing row gets origin='live' and stays visible in the live-filtered views. The offline test asserts that callers who don't pass `origin` still write 'live' (params[-3]). The DB-level test for pre-existing rows, test_migration.py::test_origin_migration_defaults_pre_existing_rows_to_live_and_keeps_them_readable, is integration-only and the gate deselected it.

Both views are recreated with `where origin = 'live'`: datapoints_read at line 24 and board_read at line 49. In board_read the filter is applied before DISTINCT ON / fetched_at desc. The unmarked DB test queries both real views and asserts they return only the live row.

`persist_datapoint` takes `origin: str = "live"` and writes it in both the INSERT column list and params, and in the UPDATE. The offline test asserts that the statement includes `origin` and that the params end with ('backfill', None, None). The DB round-trip tests at :434/:454 are integration-marked and were deselected.

This test is NOT integration-marked. It uses the real `postgres` fixture, which raises rather than skipping when no DB is available (lines 37-52). The gate reported 344 passed and no errors, so it ran against real Postgres with all migrations applied. It inserts a live row, then a backfill row fetched one minute later with a 2024 source_timestamp. It asserts the backfill row sorts later in raw datapoints, but board_read and datapoints_read return only the live row. That is a direct test of the adversarial scenario.
`uv run pytest -q` exited 0: 344 passed, 64 deselected. The integration-marked tests are excluded by addopts.

note: The work looks real, not faked: attempt 3 replaced the tautological Python simulation with an unmarked test that runs against real Postgres views, and that test ran in the gate. Remaining gaps: the declared tests/test_persist_board.py was never touched, the existing-row and 'shadow'-origin DB tests are still integration-only and were deselected, and nothing in the repo verifies the title's claim that the migration was applied to production.
